title: Another issue on Windows with ot.da.OTDA()
author: toto6

comments.author: rflamary
comments.body:
The difference between the Windows and Debian result is indeed a serious problem. I personally cannot investigate this bug because I don't have any Windows available. Could you confirm that it happens only on very large problems?

The fact that it does not sum to 1 is because the LP solver has not converged. 
It comes from the fact that we limit the number of iteration in the C code and it should be a parameters of emd function.

If you set a larger value manually, in the C code and compile manually it should work better.  We really need to do it because your are the second to ask this question.

comments.author: toto6
comments.body:
with
```
import numpy as np
import ot
a = np.random.rand(1500, 95)
b = np.random.rand(4000, 95)
opt = ot.da.OTDA()
opt.fit(a,b)
print(np.sum(opt.G))
```
it returns `1` on both Windows and Debian.
By increasing by 1000:
```
import numpy as np
import ot
a = np.random.rand(1500, 95)
b = np.random.rand(5000, 95)
opt = ot.da.OTDA()
opt.fit(a,b)
print(np.sum(opt.G))
```
it returns me `0.9992` on debian and `0` on Windows.
